hook: The inventor of the phonograph and the light bulb, with 1,093 patents to his name.

pages.x: Thomas Edison was born in 1847 in Milan, Ohio, and grew up in Port Huron, Michigan. He went to school for only a few months; when his teacher called him "addled", his mother took him out and taught him at home.
At 12 he sold newspapers and sweets on the train to Detroit, and set up a laboratory in the baggage car, until his chemicals set it on fire. As a boy he also began to go deaf.
In 1862 he snatched a three-year-old boy from the path of a train. To thank him, the boy's father, the station agent, taught him to work the telegraph, his first trade.

In 1876 he built a laboratory at Menlo Park, New Jersey, where teams of workers turned out inventions, aiming for "a minor invention every ten days and a big thing every six months". It was the first research lab of its kind.
In 1877 he made a machine that recorded sound on a cylinder wrapped in tin foil. He shouted "Mary had a little lamb" into it, and it played his voice back.
pages.fx: For the first time sound could be recorded and played again. It was the start of recorded music.

pages.x: Others had made electric lights, but they burned out fast. In 1879 his team tested thousands of materials, and found a carbon thread that glowed for many hours.
pages.fx: With his power station in New York in 1882, electric light spread to homes, streets and factories, and night changed for ever.

pages.x: He fought for his direct current against the alternating current of Westinghouse and Tesla. His side even killed animals with electricity in public to show that alternating current was deadly. Alternating current won.
His lab at West Orange built the Kinetoscope, a box for watching short films through a peephole, and the first film studio, a black hut that turned to follow the Sun.
pages.fx: They helped start the film industry.

pages.x: "Genius is one per cent inspiration and ninety-nine per cent perspiration," he said. He often worked through the night and slept in short naps on his lab bench.
Edison's inventions brought electric light, recorded sound and films into everyday life, and his research lab became the model for modern industry.
pts: Made the light bulb practical and built the first power station
